about.heading: More than a manufacturer.
paragraphs: Strategic Trust for Advanced and Reliable Knowledge (STARK) provides integrated manufacturing solutions across woodworks, furniture and mattresses, for hospitality, residential, commercial, administrative, healthcare, government, educational and mixed-use projects.

It was formed in 2026, when Saudi Light Industries, making foam and mattresses in Jeddah since 1967, joined with Trust Wood and the Haidar family's decades in the wood industry. Two factories, one company.

That is why design, manufacturing and on-site execution sit in a single accountable process here rather than across four contracts. Every element is engineered for durability and finished to the standard hospitality demands.

process.heading: Our Process
process.sub: From the first drawing to the installed room, the same six steps, inside one company.

steps.title: Design
steps.body: Drawings, mood boards and materials worked through with the client until the drawing is the thing that gets built.

steps.title: Engineering
steps.body: Shop drawings and technical detail: the design resolved into parts, fixings and tolerances a machine can run.

steps.title: Value Engineering
steps.body: Alternatives costed against the specification, so savings come out of the method and not out of the approved finish.

steps.title: Manufacturing
steps.body: Cut, sized, moulded, assembled and finished on automated lines inside our own factories.

steps.title: Quality Assurance
steps.body: Every stage checked against a written quality plan with stated tolerances, rather than against a fitter's judgement.

steps.title: Delivery & Installation
steps.body: Delivered and installed by our own teams. The project ends when the space is ready, not when the truck leaves.

turnkey.heading: From Design to Installation
turnkey.sub: Most projects don't fail because of capability. They fail because responsibility is fragmented across multiple suppliers.
turnkey.promise: STARK brings every capability under one roof with one contract, one consistent standard, and one accountable partner responsible for the final outcome.

features.title: One accountable partner
features.body: Design, production and site work sit under a single contract, so nothing falls into a gap between trades.

features.title: Made to measure
features.body: Every element is drawn for the room it will stand in and built to those dimensions, so the piece fits the space rather than the space being altered to take the piece.

features.title: One quality standard
features.body: The same stage-gated checks apply to a wood element, a piece of furniture and a mattress.

features.title: Delivered, not shipped
features.body: Coordinated delivery and installation. The project ends when the space is ready, not when the truck leaves.

hero.sub: STARK's woodworks division takes a project from raw panel to installed interior: engineered joinery, fitted furniture and full interior fit-outs, produced on our own lines and installed by our own teams.
hero.alt: Machined timber on the production line.

capabilities.heading: From design intent to crafted execution.
capabilities.sub: Volume production and bespoke joinery are usually different businesses. Running both on the same lines is what lets a single project keep one standard from the lobby to the last guest room.

items.title: Automated production lines
items.body: Doors, panels and solid timber each run on their own line: programmed cutting, edge work and through-boring, then an automated paint line and a packing section. Repeatability is what makes a large fit-out possible without a drop in finish.
items.alt: Panels running through the automated production line.

items.title: Conditioned before it is cut
items.body: Timber is seasoned in a dry-air chamber and held in a climatic chamber before machining, and the seasoning is checked twice a day. In this climate that step is the difference between joinery that stays shut and joinery that moves through its first summer.

items.title: Finishing in-house
items.body: A finishing line, a profile sander and a 6 x 12 m water-wash spray booth, under our own roof and on our own schedule. Nothing waits in a queue at a third-party shop, and nothing arrives on site with a finish nobody signed off.

services.heading: Integrated solutions, delivered end to end.
services.sub: Most interiors are assembled from separate suppliers who each own a piece and none of the outcome. These sit under one name.

standards.heading: Every stage is inspected, and the allowance is written down.
standards.sub: This is the quality plan our factory works to. Each stage names the equipment, the document it is checked against and who signs it off. Inspection is 100% of production unless the stage says otherwise.

rows.check: Weighed and measured against the purchase order and the technical specification
Dry-air chamber, checked twice a day against the seasoning procedure
Automatic saw, cut to drawing with a 10 mm machining allowance
CNC, sized to drawing with a 5 mm allowance
Moulded to drawing with a 3 mm allowance
Assembled to drawing with a 2 mm allowance
Paint chamber, finished to drawing with a 2 mm allowance
Worked to the work-order instructions and signed off by the section head
Inspected against the drawing, and the report is signed by the quality manager with the client's representative

hero.sub: STARK manufactures mattresses for two very different customers, through two focused brands: one built for the home, one built for hotels that replace a floor at a time.
hero.alt: A blue mattress on a low wooden bed, against a veined stone headboard wall.

brands.heading: One manufacturing standard. Two comfort identities.
brands.sub: A family choosing a bed once a decade and a hotel replacing two hundred of them need different products, different warranties and different conversations. Pretending otherwise is how one of them ends up badly served.

items.name: blue mattress
items.body: STARK's specialised mattress brand, created for modern homes, hospitality projects, healthcare environments and commercial spaces. Its models run from cooling comfort and motion isolation to natural latex, recovery support and customisable firmness.
items.alt: A blue mattress on a wooden platform bed in a bright bedroom.

items.name: siesta mattresses
items.body: STARK's established mattress brand, built for homes, hotels and commercial environments. Spring, foam, memory foam, orthopaedic and hospitality mattresses across a range of comfort levels and price points, with warranties of up to 10 years on selected models.
items.alt: A hotel bedroom with an upholstered headboard and bedside lamps.

models.heading: Eight models, one line.
models.sub: Each model is a different combination of springs, foams and comfort layers. The names are blue's own.
models.note: siesta's range is not shown here: there is no siesta product photography yet.

techItems.name: Memory Foam
techItems.body: Body-contouring comfort for pressure relief and support.

techItems.name: Natural Latex
techItems.body: Organic latex for durability and natural comfort.

techItems.name: Pocket Springs
techItems.body: Motion isolation and adaptive support for shared sleep.

techItems.name: TPE Support
techItems.body: An adaptive layer that distributes weight and eases pressure points.

techItems.name: Custom Comfort
techItems.body: Adjustable firmness for personalised sleep preferences.

engineering.heading: The same four layers, every model.
engineering.sub: A siesta mattress is built in four blocks, top to bottom. What changes between models is what goes inside each one.

items.title: Top quilted layers
items.body: Fabric, fibre and super-soft foam, quilted into one surface. This is what you feel first, and on the hospitality range it is where the fire-resistant fabric sits.

items.title: The core
items.body: Pocket springs or Bonnell springs depending on the model, with a foam border around the perimeter and a felt layer between the springs and everything above them. The core sets support; the border is what decides whether the usable area matches the size on the label.

items.title: Comfort layers
items.body: What sits between the core and the sleeper: memory foam, mini pocket springs, high-density or polyurethane layers, combined differently in each model. This is where pressure at the shoulder and the hip is dealt with.

items.title: Bottom quilted layers
items.body: The underside is built the same way and finished in an anti-slip fabric, so the mattress wears evenly and stays where it is put.

credentials.heading: The Kingdom's first foam factory.
credentials.sub: STARK is the modern face of Saudi Light Industries, the Kingdom's first foam and mattress factory, established in 1967.
credentials.reach: Sold through retail points of sale and distribution partners across the Kingdom, and supplied directly to hospitality and healthcare projects.

items.title: Founded in 1967
items.body: The first foam factory in the Kingdom, started by 15 people in a 6,000 m² plant, making foam mattresses and pillows.

items.title: Re-equipped in 1998
items.body: An assembly line was added and the factory re-equipped with Italian and German technology, which is what turned a foam maker into somewhere a hotel order can be produced consistently.

items.title: Hotel rooms since 2017
items.body: The factory extended into designing, manufacturing and equipping hotel rooms on Italian automated carpentry machines. The bed and the room around it come from the same group.

items.title: Fire-resistant for hospitality
items.body: Every model in the hospitality range is built on fire-resistant fabric, cotton or striped jacquard depending on the model.

turnkey.heading: The rest of the room, too.
turnkey.sub: Most hospitality buyers are not just buying beds. STARK's woodworks and fit-out divisions deliver the rest of the room under the same contract.

mataf.title: Mataf Extension
mataf.subtitle: Saudi Binladin Group · Makkah
mataf.headline: Interior architectural woodwork, approved on submittal
mataf.paragraph: Our woodworks factory was accepted as the supplier for interior architectural woodwork on the Mataf Extension, on a material submittal reviewed by Dar Al-Handasah and returned approved as noted.
mataf.overlaySummary: This is a material approval. It records that our woodwork was reviewed against the project specification and accepted, which is a different and more checkable thing than a finished-project photograph.

royalArts.title: King Salman Park
royalArts.subtitle: Royal Arts Complex, CP04 · Riyadh
royalArts.headline: Prequalified for the wood package
royalArts.paragraph: Our woodworks factory was submitted as the wood-work subcontractor on CP04, the Royal Arts Complex, and returned approved as noted by the project management team.
royalArts.overlaySummary: Prequalification is the stage where a project's management team checks a factory's licences, quality standards and previous work before it may be contracted. This one was recommended and accepted.

ngha.title: NGHA Specialized Hospitals
ngha.subtitle: National Guard Health Affairs · Jeddah
ngha.headline: Approved millworks supplier for two hospitals
ngha.paragraph: Our woodworks factory was submitted for millworks on the National Guard Health Affairs hospital programme, covering the Neuroscience and Traumacare Center and the King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Specialized Hospital for Children, and accepted by the engineer.
ngha.overlaySummary: Healthcare projects run some of the tightest material and documentation requirements of any sector. The vendor submittal was returned accepted, conditional on delivered items complying with the project specification.

overlaySpecs.label: Status
overlaySpecs.value: Vendor submittal approved except as noted

blueSky.title: Sky
blueSky.subtitle: blue mattress · Memory foam
blueSky.headline: Foam that takes the shape, then gives it back
blueSky.paragraph: Sky is built on high-density memory foam that adapts to the shape of the body and to how weight sits across it, easing the load on the joints and the spine. The same layer absorbs movement, so one sleeper turning over is not felt by the other.
blueSky.materials: Memory foam comfort layer, ventilated cover
blueSky.overlaySummary: The woodworks entries in this gallery are approved submittals for named developments. This is not one. Sky is a mattress in blue's 2026 catalogue, photographed by the manufacturer, and nothing here claims a client, a site or a completion.

bluePureLatex.title: Pure Latex
bluePureLatex.subtitle: blue mattress · Organic latex
bluePureLatex.headline: Latex that is certified rather than described
bluePureLatex.paragraph: Pure Latex is made from 100% natural organic latex, grown without chemical fertilisers, growth regulators or pesticides. It carries the Global Organic Latex Standard certificate and meets Oeko-Tex Standard 100 Class 01, the class written for products intended for babies.
bluePureLatex.materials: Organic latex core, Oeko-Tex certified cover
bluePureLatex.overlaySummary: Certificates are the reason this model is here. GOLS and Oeko-Tex are both registries a buyer can check, which is a different kind of claim from a description of how a mattress feels.

blueComfyZone.title: Comfy Zone
blueComfyZone.subtitle: blue mattress · Adjustable firmness
blueComfyZone.headline: Two firmness settings inside one mattress
blueComfyZone.paragraph: Comfy Zone can be changed between medium-firm and medium-soft at any point in its life, rather than being chosen once in a showroom. On a double, each side is set on its own, so two people who disagree about firmness do not have to settle it.
blueComfyZone.overlaySummary: The adjustment is the product. Most mattresses ask the buyer to predict what they will want for a decade; this one lets both sides of a double change their mind, which is the kind of feature worth photographing rather than describing.

specializedDoors.title: Doors & Panels
specializedDoors.subtitle: Product range · Custom Wood Works
specializedDoors.headline: Doors made to a performance rating, not only to a finish
specializedDoors.paragraph: Manufactured wood doors, panels and customized interior elements. Doors, panels and solid timber each run on their own line: programmed cutting, edge work and through-boring, then an automated paint line. The range covers fire-rated, non-fire-rated and acoustic doors.
specializedDoors.overlaySummary: This entry describes a manufacturing capability rather than a delivered project. It names no client and no site: it is what the door and panel lines produce, and the specification a project would be quoted against.

overlaySpecs.label: Applications
overlaySpecs.value: Interior doors, wall panels, custom elements

overlaySpecs.label: Production
overlaySpecs.value: Programmed cutting, edge work, automated paint line

interiorCladding.title: Interior Cladding
interiorCladding.subtitle: Product range · Custom Wood Works
interiorCladding.headline: Wall surfaces that arrive as a system, not as loose boards
interiorCladding.paragraph: Wall cladding, decorative surfaces and architectural wood finishes, produced to a project's setting-out drawings so panels arrive numbered and in sequence. Cladding is where tolerance work shows: the joints are the design.
interiorCladding.overlaySummary: This entry describes a manufacturing capability rather than a delivered project. Cladding is quoted from the architect's setting-out, so what is shown here is the product type and the finish options, not a room that has been handed over.

overlaySpecs.label: Sequencing
overlaySpecs.value: Numbered and sequenced to project drawings

kitchensWardrobes.title: Kitchens & Wardrobes
kitchensWardrobes.subtitle: Product range · Custom Wood Works
kitchensWardrobes.headline: The fitted work a room is judged by
kitchensWardrobes.paragraph: Functional wood products for residential, hospitality and commercial spaces: kitchens, wardrobes and vanity units built to the room's own dimensions rather than to a catalogue size.
kitchensWardrobes.materials: Panel, solid timber and applied finishes
kitchensWardrobes.overlaySummary: This entry describes a manufacturing capability rather than a delivered project. Fitted furniture is made to a surveyed opening, so the product is the specification and the tolerance, not a particular kitchen.

outdoorStructures.title: Outdoor Structures
outdoorStructures.subtitle: Product range · Custom Wood Works
outdoorStructures.headline: Wood that has to survive the weather it is placed in
outdoorStructures.paragraph: Bungalows, outdoor features and wooden structures for private and project environments. Outdoor work is a different material problem from interior joinery: the specification is chosen for movement and exposure before it is chosen for appearance.
outdoorStructures.overlaySummary: This entry describes a manufacturing capability rather than a delivered project. Outdoor timber is specified against exposure and movement, so what is shown is the product type rather than a structure that has been installed.

retailStands.title: Retail Stands
retailStands.subtitle: Product range · Custom Wood Works
retailStands.headline: Display units that carry someone else's brand
retailStands.paragraph: Custom display units and branded wood structures for commercial use. Retail work runs to a shorter programme than fit-out and to a tighter finish tolerance, because the customer stands close enough to touch it.
retailStands.materials: Panel, solid timber and applied graphics
retailStands.overlaySummary: This entry describes a manufacturing capability rather than a delivered project. Retail units are made to a brand's own guidelines, so the product here is the build standard, not a stand in a particular store.

overlaySpecs.label: Programme
overlaySpecs.value: Short runs at a tight finish tolerance

looseFurniture.title: Loose Furniture
looseFurniture.subtitle: Product range · Furniture manufacturing
looseFurniture.headline: Furniture that is delivered, not built into the wall
looseFurniture.paragraph: Comprehensive furniture manufacturing for interior and exterior applications, with diverse materials, finishes and designs. Loose furniture is the half of the wood package that arrives finished and is placed, rather than fixed and jointed on site.
looseFurniture.materials: Timber, panel, upholstery and applied finishes
looseFurniture.overlaySummary: This entry describes a manufacturing capability rather than a delivered project. Loose furniture is made to a project's own drawings, so what is shown is the range and the finish options rather than a room that has been furnished.

overlaySpecs.label: Products
overlaySpecs.value: Case goods, seating, tables, custom pieces

siestaRange.title: siesta
siestaRange.subtitle: Product range · Mattress division
siestaRange.headline: A wide range, built for the room it is bought for
siestaRange.paragraph: A wide mattress range serving luxury, economic and hospitality needs through practical comfort, durable construction and accessible quality. siesta and blue run to one manufacturing standard and two comfort identities.
siestaRange.overlaySummary: siesta is shown here as a range rather than as named models, because the mattress division's documented model list belongs to blue. The photographs are rooms rather than products for the same reason: nothing here should be read as a picture of a particular siesta mattress.
